q.t: How many lines does a music staff have?
q.e: Five lines (TAB has six — one per string).

q.t: On the staff, a note placed higher sounds…
q.e: Higher on the staff = higher pitch.

q.t: What clef does guitar music use?
q.e: The treble (G) clef.

q.t: The treble clef's curl marks which note?
q.e: It wraps around line 2 and names it G — that's why it's also called the G clef.

q.t: The lines from bottom to top are…
q.e: Every Good Boy Does Fine.

q.t: The spaces from bottom to top spell…
q.e: F A C E.

q.t: What are the short extra lines above or below the staff called?
q.e: Ledger lines extend the staff.

q.t: What divides the staff into bars?
q.e: Vertical bar lines.

q.t: A hollow oval with no stem is a…
q.e: 4 beats.

q.t: What does the symbol ♯ before a note do?
q.e: Sharp = one half step up.

q.t: Which note sits on the middle (3rd) line?
q.e: Lines E G B D F — the middle one is B.

q.t: Which note sits on the top line?
q.e: The 5th line is F.

q.t: Which note sits in the bottom space?
q.e: Spaces F A C E — the bottom is F.

q.t: One ledger line below the staff is…
q.e: Middle C sits on the first ledger line below.

q.t: What does a natural sign ♮ do?
q.e: ♮ returns the note to its plain letter.

q.t: What does a key signature with one ♯ on the F line mean?
o: Play only the first F as F♯
q.e: A key signature applies to every note of that letter.

q.t: One sharp (F♯) in the key signature usually means the key of…
q.e: G major has just one sharp, F♯.

q.t: Guitar music is written…
o: one octave higher than it sounds
one octave lower than it sounds
q.e: It keeps the guitar's low notes on the staff.

q.t: Why does the staff use both lines and spaces?
q.e: Lines and spaces together pack more notes into a readable space.

q.t: Which tells you the note's length: its position or its shape?
q.e: Position = pitch; shape = length.

q.t: The open high e string is written…
q.e: The top space is E.

q.t: The open B string is written…
q.e: The middle line is B.

q.t: The open G string is written…
q.e: Line 2 is G — where the clef curls.

q.t: A note on the top line (F) is played on…
q.e: E → F is one fret on the high e string.

q.t: A note on line 4 (D) is played on…
q.e: B → C → C♯ → D: B string fret 3.

q.t: A note in space 3 (C) is played on…
q.e: Written C in space 3 sounds an octave lower — B string fret 1.

q.t: The open D string is written…
o: in the space just below the staff
q.e: Written D sits just under the bottom line.

q.t: Why is guitar music written an octave higher than it sounds?
o: So low notes don't need lots of ledger lines
q.e: Writing an octave up keeps most guitar notes on the staff.

q.t: What does :|| mean?
q.e: Go back to the matching ||: (or the start) and play again.

q.t: Why use a key signature instead of marking each sharp?
o: It saves writing the same sharp many times
Sharps can't be written next to notes
q.e: One mark at the start covers every F in a G-major song, and shows the key.

q.t: Ode to Joy starts E E F G. Where is the G written?
q.e: Top space E, top line F, then the space above it G.

q.t: A note on line 2 with a ♯ in front is…
q.e: Line 2 is G; ♯ raises it to G♯.

q.t: A note in space 2 with a ♭ in front is…
q.e: Space 2 is A; ♭ lowers it to A♭.

q.t: The open A string is written…
o: on the second ledger line below
on the first ledger line below
q.e: Below middle C (ledger 1) comes B, then A on ledger 2.

q.t: In G major, a note on the top line with no sign in front is played as…
q.e: The key signature makes every F an F♯.

q.t: A ♮ is written before an F in a G-major song. You play…
q.e: The natural sign cancels the key signature's sharp for that note.

q.t: How many notes (lines + spaces) fit on the five-line staff itself?
q.e: 5 lines + 4 spaces = 9.

q.t: A filled oval with a stem on the middle line is…
q.e: Filled + stem = quarter; middle line = B.

q.t: A hollow oval with a stem in the top space is…
q.e: Hollow + stem = half; top space = E.

q.t: Why tie open strings to staff positions first?
o: They give landmarks; other notes are steps from them
They are the only notes on the staff
It is required by the treble clef
q.e: Known landmarks make every other note a short step away.
